conventions.convention: An exact Hermitian block encoding has J*UJ=K/α with K self-adjoint and α>0; U itself need not be Hermitian. Forward, inverse, controlled and reflection access are separate supplied operations.
The signal reflection is 2Π−I. Scalar QSP uses the Hermitian-reflection matrix with entries x, sqrt(1−x²), sqrt(1−x²), −x; conversion from the SU(2) convention retains i^d under control.
The target is exp(−iτx), τ=αt. Its truncation is E−iO, with E real even and O real odd; the coefficient branch applies the relative phase −i.
Simulation accuracy concerns the clean-input isometry, including retained output-work leakage. It does not promise exact cleanup or full-space approximation on dirty-work inputs.

Sorted-XOR mode permits distinct sorted support supersets containing listed zeros, requires transposition-compatible supports, pads the system to 2^ceil(log₂(N+d)), and charges O(log(d+1)) location calls. Supplied in-place permutations are a separate stronger interface.
For α|t|≤ε, the wrapper returns identity. The near-optimal degree estimate applies to the nontrivial branch α|t|>ε with 0<ε<1.

The sparse lower bound concerns dyadically rounded path matrices in the row-location/value XOR model, at time πn/2, with clean-input error at most 1/3. It is not a lower bound for arbitrary block-encoding access.

load_bearing.statement: For real τ and integer d≥0, the degree-d Jacobi–Anger Chebyshev truncation has uniform error at most 2Σ(k>d)|J_k(τ)|, bounded by 2(|τ|/2)^(d+1)/((d+1)!(1−|τ|/(2(d+2)))) when |τ|/(2(d+2))<1. In the regime |τ|>ε, a passing OP4 degree exists with d=O(|τ|+ln(1/ε)/ln(e+ln(1/ε)/|τ|)).

For an exact Hermitian block encoding, each eigenvalue x=λ/α with |x|<1 has paired input/output signal bases in which U has matrix [[x,s],[s,−x]], s=sqrt(1−x²), and U* has the reverse-basis action. At |x|=1 the complement is absent; x=0 is an ordinary two-dimensional signal plane.

The standard-form qubiterate has signal eigenvalues exp(±i arccos(λ/α)), with collapsed endpoint eigenlines. Alternating U,U* and projector phases gives scalar Hermitian-reflection QSP on the paired spaces and clean compression PΦ(K/α).

For exact access or the bounded-block-error variant satisfying the algorithm's post-degree budget, rational t and 0<ε≤1, a successful execution returns a unitary dilation with clean-input isometry error at most ε from the zero-work embedding of exp(−itH). Tracing out work gives reference-system trace-distance error at most ε.

Under the stated sorted sparse XOR interface, positive entry bound h, and costed uniform preparation and exact arithmetic, a unitary clean block encodes (H⊕0)/(dh). Its actual adjoint and coherent controlled versions each use O(log(d+1)) location calls and O(1) value calls.

If ||UJ−JV||≤η for an isometry J and unitaries U,V, then ||U*J−JV*||≤η, also with references and coherent controls. For actual unitaries U_j and ideal unitaries V_j with local clean-input errors η_j, the product clean-input error is at most Ση_j.
For finite-dimensional isometries V,W:H→K⊗E with ||V−W||≤δ, every density matrix on H⊗R, for nonzero finite-dimensional R, gives reduced output trace distance at most δ.
For n≥1, the weighted parity-path matrix H_x with weights sqrt(i(n+1−i))/n has operator norm at most one and exp(−iH_xπn/2)|0,0⟩=(−i)^n|n,parity(x)⟩.
Any quantum query algorithm that, on every x∈{0,1}^n, outputs parity(x) with error at most 1/3 using the coherent XOR oracle for x makes at least n/2 oracle queries.

concerns.concern: Facts [F5] attributes to def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion the formula that |u⟩⟨v| contributes matrix entry ⟨e_i,u⟩⟨v,e_j⟩. Under the explicitly stated root convention, linear in the first argument, this equals conjugate(u_i) v_j, whereas the cited definition gives u_i conjugate(v_j). For example, u=i e_1 and v=e_1 make [F5] give −i instead of i. Proof 2.1 uses the correct overlap order, so the theorem's conclusion survives, but the Facts block contains a false coordinate identity and misstates its supplier.

Facts [F3] describes the cited sparse-no-fast-forwarding theorem as a lower bound for 'the full path family', and Proof 2.1 says the exact-weight example 'is the n=2 instance of the constant-normalization family in [F3]'. The cited theorem instead states its lower bound for the dyadically rounded matrices. At n=2 its b is 5 and q_1=q_2=23/32, giving normalization 23/16; this example uses weights 1/sqrt(2), normalization sqrt(2), and exact time-π endpoint transfer. The exact-weight calculations are sound, but the identification with the cited rounded family is false.

seams_checked.note: The sorted sparse interface preserves total XOR oracles, finite exact value codes, sentinels, and separate access costs; it does not infer in-place permutations.
Odd/even transforms, kernel terms, real extraction, normalized block error, and the 4d sqrt(block-error) robustness estimate are used with their stated qualifications.
Compression error is normalized; normalization and forward/inverse/controlled implementation costs remain separate.
Reflection signs, phase order, parity, controlled scalar phases, and successful numerical-synthesis error budgets agree. Arithmetic complexity is not promoted to Turing bit complexity.
Inverse and controlled access are explicit, and the −i coefficient phase and i^d convention conversion are retained under control.
The parity argument uses input-independent inter-query circuits and correctness on every promised input; quantum query counts remain separate from circuit generation and bit costs.

The sparse correctness theorem's [F5] reverses the root-coordinate conjugations relative to def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion. Its actual Proof 2.1 overlap is correct; the precise mismatch is recorded in concerns.
Finite spectral evolution and its unitary derivative are used with the exp(−itH) sign. Path transfer is proved locally.
XOR oracles are total involutions; compute-copy-uncompute charges reversal, and controlled XOR evaluation is constructed with ordinary queries.
Uniform preparation, its inverse, arithmetic and flag rotations are supplied and costed. No coherent loading or finite-alphabet synthesis follows from a classical table.
The complete clean projector, reflection sign, correction −WRW*RW and 10 sqrt(η) retained-leakage estimate match the robust OAA supplier.

HHL uses the sorted-XOR bridge with h=1, rationally rounds simulation times, retains actual work, and uses literal adjoints and clean-subspace hybrids. Its loose query estimate follows from the sharper QA25 bound.
CKS retains supplied-permutation and optional sorted-XOR costs, explicit finite-value budgets, clean-input simulation, actual reversals and separate phase-generation/gate hypotheses.

Sparse SDP substitution uses transposition-compatible sorted support unions with listed zeros, rational simulation-time approximation, original-label reference preparation, and clean-subspace hybrids with retained work.
